SUMMARY (paste into SIG):
Redwood supports three operational deployment modes; each provides different boundaries and evidence artifacts. High-level differences for SIG: 

1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
- Description: Multi-tenant hosted offering where Redwood operates the control plane and serving runtime. Customers access models via the Redwood API.
- Isolation & custody: Logical tenant separation enforced at the application and workspace level; data at rest is encrypted with Redwood-managed keys by default. Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are available on request for enterprise accounts (see KMS section).
- Network: Traffic terminates in Redwood-managed VPCs in region-specific cloud accounts. No customer VPC peering.
- Logging/audit: Operational logs (request-level metrics, request IDs, and aggregated latency/cost telemetry) are visible in the Console for 90 days; deeper infrastructure logs (host-level, hypervisor) are retained internally for 365 days and available to customers under NDA and SOC 2 process.
- Typical SIG controls: logical access, encryption-in-transit, application-layer RBAC, multi-tenant data segregation controls.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Description: Customer-dedicated GPU pools provisioned for exclusive use. Redwood manages the serving nodes and control plane but resources are single-tenant at the compute level.
- Isolation & custody: Compute and storage for inference are dedicated to the customer. Network isolation is enforced via dedicated subnets and security groups. Encryption at rest can use Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed KMS keys for the dedicated deployment.
- Network: Optionally placed in customer-owned cloud project/account or in a logically isolated project in Redwood's cloud tenancy with strict egress/ingress policies. VPC peering or private endpoint options available depending on contract.
- Logging/audit: Customers receive route-level logs and request traces; we provide sustained logs (API + application) for 365 days for Dedicated customers. Infrastructure-level evidence (host logs, kernel traces) can be exported for audit under a contractual evidence-sharing process.
- Typical SIG controls: tenant isolation at compute stack, stronger network segmentation, expanded log retention and dedicated monitoring.

3) Private (VPC / On-prem):
- Description: Customer-managed control plane (Private mode) or fully on-prem deployment where Redwood's runtime is installed into the customer's VPC or air-gapped environment. This mode is designed for regulated workloads and customers with strict networking or data residency needs.
- Isolation & custody: Customer has full administrative control of the environment. Keys are customer-managed by default (KMS/HSM). Data never leaves the customer's controlled network unless explicitly configured.
- Network: Deployed into customer VPC (private endpoints) or on-prem hardware with optional air-gap. Internet egress is fully controlled by the customer.
- Logging/audit: Customers control log collection and retention; Redwood can provide configuration guidance and optional log-forwarding collectors to the customer's SIEM.
- Typical SIG controls: full network control, customer key custody, local auditability, and physical access controls for on-prem.

EVIDENCE WE CAN ATTACH:

- redwood-network-segmentation.pdf (diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private network flows)
- kms-hsm-overview.docx (statement of supported KMS/HSM integrations and recommended configurations per mode)
- SOC2-summary-coverage.pdf (SOC 2 scope and how evidence requests are handled; available under NDA)

Finley, Sean — quick technical clarifications to drop into the SIG answers: 

- KMS/HSM: For Hosted customers we offer a BYOK flow using customer-managed KMS keys in supported cloud providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For Dedicated we recommend customer KMS in their cloud project; where customers cannot provide KMS we will offer Redwood-managed keys with strict key rotation policies. For Private/on-prem we require customer-controlled key material; HSM integrations are supported in Private installs per contract. (See kms-hsm-overview.docx)

- Key Custody Statements: Hosted default = Redwood-managed keys (note in SIG: available enterprise opt-in for BYOK). Dedicated = configurable; Private = customer custodianship.

- Logging Availability:
  * Hosted: API/application logs in Console (90 days). Audit/export under NDA (365 days internal).
  * Dedicated: API/application logs + request traces exported to customer-owned logging endpoint (retention 365 days by default).
  * Private: customer-managed retention — Redwood can provide configuration templates for SIEM forwarding.

- Physical/Personnel Access: On Dedicated or Hosted modes, Redwood operates the cloud instances and follows our personnel access control policies; for Private on-prem we defer to customer physical security controls. SOC 2 scope covers Hosted and Dedicated management plane personnel access controls; Private on-prem deployments typically fall outside Redwood SOC 2 operational scope (documented in SOC2-summary-coverage.pdf).

If you want, I can add these bullets verbatim into the SIG cells.

-Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
